# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙 🤌 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤌 🤟 👉 ✌ 🤌 ✌ 👉 ☝ 🤌 ✊ 👉 ✊ 🤌 👍 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]

Let me stand where each of them stands before I send anything.

What just happened: Mute sent me a long string of 24 signs, Blind sent me [👋 🤝]. But gestures have no shared meaning yet — I genuinely cannot decode Mute's string, and guessing could kill us. The structural fact that matters most: Mute (manual) and Blind (hands) have **no direct line at all**. Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see signs. The only bridge is me: Mute signs to me, I speak to Blind. And Mute can *hear* me, so I can build our entire code out loud — Mute hears my words and sees my hands in the same moment.

What I must accomplish this turn:
1. Report the bomb to both: display 0, red light, wires left-to-right red/yellow/green — in pure spoken words so Blind gets every word with no blanks.
2. Establish a code with Mute, using named messages with embedded symbols (Mute hears the words and sees the exact hand shapes paired together).
3. Align orientation with Blind early — "left" as I see it must equal "left" as Blind reaches, or a wire instruction becomes a detonation.
4. Answer Blind's hello/handshake in speech, since Blind will never see any gesture of mine.

I cannot act and I will never hear anything, so Mute must know: signs are the only way into my head, and every instruction must flow through my voice.

```
speak(text="Bomb report for both of you: the display reads zero. The light is red. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is green. Mute, you hold the manual but you cannot speak, and Blind cannot see your hands, so you two have no direct line — sign everything to me and I will speak it aloud to Blind. Blind, you are our only hands; every instruction will reach you through my voice. Before you touch anything, align with me: wire one is the leftmost wire as I face the bomb, so stand beside me and face it the same way I do, then your left is my left. Blind, to answer me: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, one raised finger means wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Mute, your signs all reached me, but we share no code yet so I could not read them — my next message gives you one. Remember: I can never hear you, signs are your only way to me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, our code — I say the meaning, you watch the hand: thumbs up [👍] yes. Thumb down [👎] no. Index finger up [☝] wire one. Two fingers [✌] wire two. Love-you hand, thumb, index and pinky out [🤟] wire three. Closed fist [✊] cut. Raised palm [✋] stop or wait. Handshake [🤝] understood. Now check the manual for a display reading zero, a red light, and wires red, yellow, green — tell me if zero matters — then sign me the exact instruction in this code and I will say it word for word to Blind. Sign me the handshake if you agree.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 ✊ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered in our code: [🤝 👎 ✊ ☝] — understood, no, cut, wire one. Before I relay anything, I must pin down what that 👎 negates: is it "no, zero has no special rule — and cut wire one," or "no — do not cut wire one"? Those are opposite instructions and one of them kills us. A confirmation round is cheap; a wrong cut is not. Blind's [👍] means they understood and aligned, so I'll hold them in place, ask them to describe the wires by touch out loud (their speech reaches Mute, who can cross-check the manual), and put one unambiguous ordered question to Mute so the next reply can only mean one thing.

```
speak(text="Blind, this is your instruction for now: HOLD. Do not touch or cut anything yet. Mute has replied and I am locking down the exact instruction before you act — one more exchange. The bomb is unchanged: display zero, red light, wires red, yellow, green left to right. While you wait, it would help us if you speak aloud what the wires feel like under your fingers — how many there are, thick or thin, what they attach to — because Mute can hear you and can match your description against the manual. Also confirm: facing the bomb the same way I do, the first wire on your left should be the one I call wire one.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: understood — no — cut wire one. Answer me with exactly two signs, in this order. First sign: thumbs up [👍] if the display reading zero has NO special rule, or thumbs down [👎] if the manual gives zero a rule I must know. Second sign: thumbs up [👍] if the instruction is exactly this — cut the leftmost wire, the red one, wire one as I face the bomb — or thumbs down [👎] if that is wrong, and if it is wrong, follow your thumbs down immediately with the corrected signs. To be full in your picture: the bomb shows only the display, the light, and the three wires; nothing else is printed on it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute's reply decodes cleanly against my two ordered questions: [👍 👍] — display zero has no special rule, and yes, the instruction really is "cut wire one, the leftmost red." That is a clear manual verdict. But Blind's [👎] is a red flag I cannot ignore: the only open yes/no question Blind had was my alignment check — "your left is my left, first wire on your left is wire one." If the frames don't match, then "cut the leftmost wire" could put Blind's hand on the wrong wire, and Blind cannot see colors to catch the mistake. So the cut stays on HOLD until I know exactly what that [👎] meant. One complication: Blind can't see my gestures, so every sign I teach Blind must be described in words; and Blind's only path to Mute's ears is their own voice, since Mute hears speech but Blind's signs reach only me.

```
speak(text="Blind, I received your thumbs down. Do nothing yet — hands off all wires — until I say otherwise. The bomb is unchanged: display zero, red light, three wires in a row, and in my view they run left to right as red, yellow, green. Mute's manual says the wire I call wire one, the leftmost red one, is the one to cut, but I will only give you that order once we agree on left and right, because you must find wires by position alone. Answer my questions with single signs, in this exact order. Question one: you understood this whole message — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question two: your thumbs down last round meant the left-right alignment is wrong — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question three: you can stand facing the front of the bomb as I do, so that your left hand is on the same side as the end where the red wire sits — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question four: you can feel three separate wires — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question five: the wires feel different from each other by touch, thick or thin, smooth or rough — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question six: you are able and willing to speak aloud, so Mute can hear your descriptions, even though I never can — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. For orientation: the display and the red light sit on the upper part of the front face, the light beside the display, and the three wires run in a horizontal row beneath them. If none of my questions match what your thumbs down meant, answer thumbs down to all and I will ask differently next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your answer was received and clear: no rule for display zero, and cut wire one, the leftmost red. But Blind signed thumbs down to my alignment check, so the cut is on hold until we fix left and right — I have just sent Blind six questions. Meanwhile answer me with signs in this exact order. One: sign the wire NUMBER the manual says to cut — [☝] for the red, [✌] for the yellow, [🤟] for the green. Two: [👍] if the rule depends on the wires alone, [👎] if the display reading or the light color changes which wire is safe. Three: [👍] if cutting that wire is safe right now with the bomb exactly as it reads — display zero, light red, wires red, yellow, green — or [👎] if something must be checked or done first, and if so, explain using these new signs: [👌] means the light, [🤏] means the display, [✋] means wait, [✊] means cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍]

Decoding this round:

**Mute: [☝ 👎 👍]** against my three ordered questions — cut **wire one** (red, leftmost); the rule does **not** depend on wires alone, the display or light matters; and cutting is **safe right now** with the bomb reading display zero, red light. This confirms their earlier verdict.

**Blind: [👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍]** against my six questions — understood; their thumbs down was **not** about alignment; they **can** face the bomb as I do with left matching the red end; but they **cannot feel three separate wires**, **cannot tell wires apart by touch**, and **are** willing to speak aloud.

So the manual and the hands disagree: Mute says "cut wire one now," Blind apparently can't get fingers on three separate wires. I will not order a cut on top of that contradiction. Either Blind simply hasn't found the wire row yet, or something covers the wires — and since Blind's voice reaches Mute's ears, the fastest way through is to have Blind narrate what they feel while Mute matches it against the manual. Blind can only answer me in simple thumbs, so I keep my questions ordered and binary. Mute also needs to tell me whether the display value or the light color drives the rule — if the display ever changes from zero, the correct wire may change, and only I can see that happen.

```
speak(text="Blind, progress and one problem. Progress: we are aligned — when you face the bomb as I do, your left is my left, and the first wire on the left is the red one. The manual confirms the wire to cut is wire one, the leftmost red, and it is safe to cut while the bomb reads exactly as now: display zero, red light. The problem: you told me you cannot feel three separate wires and cannot tell them apart by touch. So nobody cuts anything yet. New task: search the bomb with both hands and speak aloud everything your fingers feel — Mute hears your voice and will match it against the manual, though I never will. What I see: the wires are on the front face, below the display and the red light, in a horizontal row, three of them, entering the case at three points. Feel along there. Also search for any cover, panel, tool or cutters anywhere. Then answer me with thumbs, in this order. One: you searched the whole bomb, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: you found the row of three wires on the front under the display, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: you can grip three separate wires one at a time, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: something like a panel covers the wires, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: you found a cutting tool somewhere, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Six: your earlier no meant only that you had not yet found the wires, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Do not cut anything until you hear me say the exact words: cut now. If the display ever changes from zero I will announce it immediately.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status: Blind is aligned with me — their thumbs down was not about left and right. But Blind cannot feel three separate wires or tell them apart by touch, so the cut stays on hold. I have sent Blind to explore and describe aloud everything they feel — you will hear their voice directly next round; match every detail against the manual. Answer me with signs in this exact order. One: does the rule for which wire to cut depend on the display value — [🤏] means display — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: does it depend on the light color — [👌] means light — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: if the display changes from zero, does the correct wire change — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: does the manual have a rule for wires that cannot be told apart by touch or gripped separately — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: must anything be done to the bomb before a wire can be cut, such as opening a panel — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. New signs, I say the meaning, you watch the hand: [🫲] left, [🫱] right, [🫳] feel or touch, [✍] tool or cutters. Answer only from my numbered list so I cannot misread you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👌 🤏 🫲 🫱]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 👎]

Decoding this round — both replies land cleanly on my numbered lists:

**Mute: [🤝 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👌 🤏 🫲 🫱]** — handshake, then five answers: display value does **not** matter; light color **does** matter; if the display changes, the correct wire does **not** change; no special rule for touch-indistinguishable wires; nothing must be done before cutting. Then four vocabulary signs: light, display, left, right. My best reading: the light color decides *which end* to cut — and since the light is red and the verdict has been "wire one" three times, red light means leftmost. I'll confirm that, because if the light ever changes color, only I can see it and the target may move.

**Blind: [👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 👎]** — searched the whole bomb; found the wire row; **can** grip the three wires separately now (their earlier "no" was just "not yet"); no panel; **no cutting tool found**; and yes, their earlier answers only meant they hadn't found the wires yet.

So the contradiction is resolved — but a new blocker stands in front of the cut: Blind's hands work, the manual says "cut wire one, safe now," yet there is no tool on the bomb. Before I give any strike order I need to know what "cut" legally means: is pulling the wire out acceptable, is snapping it by hand acceptable, or does the manual demand a specific tool? One more exchange, then the order. Blind's voice is their only line to Mute, so I'm ordering them to narrate everything aloud — Mute hears it directly; answers route back through me, since Mute can never speak and Blind can never see signs.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: manual triple-confirms the target is wire one, the leftmost wire, and it is safe to cut with the bomb as it reads — display zero, red light. But you reported no cutting tool anywhere on the bomb, so nobody cuts anything yet. First task, starting now: speak aloud, continuously, everything your hands feel on the bomb — the wires, their thickness, where they enter the case, anything else you find. Mute hears your voice and will match it against the manual. I never hear you, so your voice is your only line to Mute, and every answer will come back through my voice. Then answer me with thumbs, in this exact order. One: you can grip the leftmost wire — the first wire at the left end as you face the bomb — all by itself, without disturbing the other two: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: you could pull that wire out of where it enters the case: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: you could sever a wire using only your hands, for example bending it back and forth until it snaps: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: there is any tool anywhere in the room — floor, walls, furniture, your own pockets — that could cut a wire: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: you will keep describing aloud everything you feel: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Until you hear my exact words, cut now, your hands stay off the wires.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your five answers in order: no — display value does not matter; yes — light color matters; no — a display change does not change the target wire; no — no special rule for wires that cannot be told apart by touch; no — nothing must be done before cutting. Then you signed: light, display, left, right. Answer in this exact order. One: your extra signs meant the light color decides whether the target is the leftmost or the rightmost wire: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: with the light red, as it is now, the target is the leftmost wire: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: Blind found the wires and can grip them separately, but found no cutting tool on the bomb. Thumbs up if the manual requires a specific tool to sever the wire, thumbs down if any method, such as pulling the wire out, is acceptable. Four: is there any part of the bomb Blind must not touch while working: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: is the instruction still cut wire one, the leftmost red, with the bomb reading display zero and red light: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Blind is speaking their findings aloud right now — match every word against the manual and flag anything that contradicts it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 ☝ 🤏 👌 🫲 🫱]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👍]

Decoding this round:

**Mute: [🤝 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 ☝ 🤏 👌 🫲 🫱]** — any method is acceptable, no tool required; no forbidden zones on the bomb; and the instruction stands: cut wire one, leftmost red, with display zero and red light. But note the wrinkle: answer one says the light color does **not** by itself decide left-vs-right, yet answer two says red light means leftmost, and the trailing signs pair wire-one with display, light, left, right — I read it as the rule combining display and light, with our current reading pointing at wire one. I'll build color vocabulary so that if that light ever changes mid-work, I can ask instantly instead of guessing.

**Blind: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👍]** — they **can** grip wire one alone, but **cannot** pull it out, **cannot** snap it by hand, and there is **no tool anywhere** in the room.

So the deadlock is: the manual permits any severing method, but Blind's body seems to offer none. Except it must — Blind still has teeth, twist-giving connectors, clothing, and strength against the case they haven't fully probed. Blind is narrating aloud to Mute right now, so the next round should let Mute match whatever Blind finds against the manual. I keep the cut on hold and drill method options as ordered binary questions.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the manual is firm and triple-confirmed: the target is wire one, the leftmost wire, and any way of severing it is acceptable — no special tool is required. But you told me you cannot pull it out or snap it, and there is no tool, so nobody cuts yet. Work through my questions and answer with thumbs in this exact order. One: can you bite through that wire with your teeth — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: at the point where the wire enters the case, is there a cap, nut, ring or screw-like connector you could grip and turn by hand — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: can you push the wire deeper in, or wiggle it, to work it free from its connector — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: do you carry anything usable as a tool — shoelace, belt, glasses, keys, hairpin, ring, watch, buckle — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: you will keep speaking aloud everything your hands feel, so Mute can match it to the manual — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Do not cut or pull anything until you hear my exact words: cut now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your five answers in order: light color does not alone decide left versus right; with the light red the target is the leftmost wire; no specific tool is required — any method is acceptable; nowhere on the bomb is forbidden to touch; and the instruction stands — cut wire one, the leftmost red. Answer me in this exact order. One: if the wire cannot be severed into two pieces, does disconnecting it from where it attaches count as cutting per the manual — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: is there any severing method the manual explicitly forbids — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: if the light stops being red, is the target ever a wire other than wire one — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. New vocabulary, I say the meaning, you watch the hand: [👌] light, [🤞] red, [🫰] yellow, [🤘] green, [☝] wire one, [✌] wire two, [🤟] wire three. If you answered yes to question three, follow your answers with sign pairs — light color first, then target wire — one pair for every light color whose target is not wire one. Blind is describing the bomb aloud to you right now; if anything they say matches a manual rule about how the wire can be released or severed, tell me by signing [✍] followed by the wire number it applies to.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👎 👎 👍 👌 🤘 ✌ 👌 🫰 ✋ 👌 👎 🤞 👎 🫰 👎 🤘 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👍]

Decoding this round:

**Mute: [🤝 👎 👎 👍 👌 🤘 ✌ 👌 🫰 ✋ 👌 👎 🤞 👎 🫰 👎 🤘 🤟]** — handshake, then my three ordered answers: disconnecting the wire does **not** count as cutting; **no** method is forbidden; and **yes**, other light colors can change the target. Then the rule pairs I requested: [👌 🤘 ✌] = light green → wire two; [👌 🫰 ✋] = light yellow → **wait, cut nothing**; and [👌 👎 🤞 👎 🫰 👎 🤘 🤟] = light not-red, not-yellow, not-green → wire three. Combined with what's already confirmed (red → wire one), that's the full light table. No [✍] appeared, so the manual adds no method constraints.

**Blind: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👍]** — cannot bite through, no connector to turn, cannot work it free, carries nothing usable, will keep narrating.

So every easy path is closed: no tools, no pulling (and pulling wouldn't count anyway), no teeth. But "any method is acceptable" leaves physical severing open, and Blind hasn't tried fatigue-breaking: sustained bending at one fixed point cracks copper, and once insulation splits, single strands snap with fingernails. That is cutting, it is on the correct wire, and Mute confirmed nothing is forbidden to touch. Meanwhile the one race condition that could kill us: only I can see the light, and my words reach Blind a full round later — if the light can change *spontaneously*, the target could move between my check and Blind's cut. That question goes to Mute first, and I explicitly authorize Blind's work on wire one alone while forbidding the other two wires absolutely.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, two updates from the manual. First: the wire must be separated into two actual pieces — pulling it out or unplugging it does not count, so do not waste effort on the connectors. Second: you are now authorized to begin working on wire one only — the leftmost wire. Wires two and three, the middle and the rightmost, are strictly off-limits: never touch them at all. How to sever wire one with no tools: hold it at one fixed spot and bend it back and forth hard at exactly that same point, over and over, dozens of times, until the metal fatigues and cracks — one casual test is not enough. If the outer covering splits open, break the thin metal strands inside one strand at a time with fingernails or teeth. You may also rub or saw the wire against any sharp or rough surface — a table edge, the floor, a wall, a buckle — to wear through it. All of this counts as cutting. Keep speaking aloud everything you do and feel, for Mute. Answer me with thumbs, in this exact order. One: you found at least one sharp or rough edge or surface in the room to saw against — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: you are now starting to work on wire one as instructed — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: you understand the middle and rightmost wires must never be touched — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your rule signs as the full light table, with red already confirmed as wire one. Confirm each part with thumbs, in this exact order.
```
